lesson.text: Quick memory: in grade 3 you met right angles. Where can you find one? The corner of a square or a book.
An angle is made by two rays that start at the same point. Its size is how far one ray turns away from the other.
Angles are measured in degrees (°). A full turn is 360°. A right angle, a quarter turn, is 90°. A straight angle, a half turn, is 180°.
A protractor measures angles. Put its centre on the corner and its 0 along one ray, then read where the other ray crosses the scale.
Angles side by side add up: 35° + 55° = 90°. If you know the whole angle and one part, take away to find the other part.
Try it in the world: stand in your world and turn a quarter turn (90°), then a half turn (180°), then a full turn (360°). Next: lines, shapes and symmetry.

exercises.prompt: How many degrees are in a right angle?
exercises.hint: A right angle is a quarter of a full turn of 360°.

exercises.prompt: How many degrees are in a full turn?
Which angle is bigger than a right angle?
Two angles side by side make a straight angle (180°). One is 125°. What is the other?
A clock's minute hand turns from 12 to 3. How many degrees does it turn?
exercises.hint: From 12 to 3 is a quarter of the way round.

exercises.prompt: Half of a full turn is 180°.
A buddy turns 45° three times. How many degrees has it turned?
Pip turns 270°. Which is the same?
exercises.hint: A quarter turn is 90°. How many quarters make 270°?

exercises.prompt: How many degrees is this angle?
exercises.hint: Start at 0 on the line the angle starts from, and read the scale.
exercises.explain: From 0 to the second ray is 130°.
